description: Nicotiana tabacum: a tall annual with very large leaves.

diseases.name: Blue Mold
diseases.description: A water-mould disease of tobacco leaves that can spread rapidly through a region.
diseases.causes: Spores blow long distances on the wind; cool, wet, cloudy weather favours infection.
symptoms: Yellow spots on the upper leaf
Blue-grey downy spores on the underside
Spots merge, leaves pucker and die
diseases.effect: Leaves are destroyed; seedbeds can be wiped out.

steps.title: Remove infected plants in seedbeds
steps.instruction: Pick off infected plants in seedbeds when the plants are dry and take them away.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered product for blue mold on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

lifecycle: Spores blow in on the wind.
Cool, wet weather lets them infect.
Yellow spots form, blue-grey spores below.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: tobacco blue mold

diseases.name: Brown Spot
diseases.description: A fungal leaf spot of mature tobacco leaves with ringed brown spots.
diseases.causes: Spores survive on debris and spread by wind; mature, lower leaves in warm, wet weather are infected.
symptoms: Round brown spots with concentric rings
A yellow halo round each spot
diseases.untreated: Heavy losses in warm, wet seasons.

steps.title: Remove lower spotted leaves
steps.instruction: Pick off lower spotted leaves when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Harvest leaves on time
steps.instruction: Do not leave mature leaves on the plant too long.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

lifecycle: Wind carries spores to mature leaves.
Brown ringed spots with halos form.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: tobacco brown spot
Content: general plant-pathology knowledge (APS disease compendia, university extension guides, UC IPM); not reviewed by a plant pathologist.

diseases.name: Frogeye Leaf Spot
diseases.description: A fungal leaf spot of tobacco with small white-centred spots.
diseases.causes: Spores spread by wind and rain from debris and infected leaves in warm, humid weather.
symptoms: Small round spots with white to grey centres
A brown border round each spot
Many spots on mature lower leaves
diseases.untreated: Heavy spotting cuts yield and quality.

steps.title: Remove spotted lower leaves
steps.instruction: Pick off spotted lower leaves when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Harvest on time
steps.instruction: Do not leave ripe leaves in the field.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

lifecycle: Spores spread in warm, humid weather.
White-centred spots form on ripe leaves.
New spores spread up the plant.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: tobacco frogeye leaf spot
Content: general plant-pathology knowledge (APS disease compendia, university extension guides, UC IPM); not reviewed by a plant pathologist.

diseases.name: Tobacco Mosaic
diseases.description: A very stable, contagious virus that mottles and distorts tobacco leaves.
diseases.causes: Spreads by contact: hands, tools and clothing; it survives for years in debris and dried leaf. No insect is needed.
symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic on the leaves
Plants stunted; sometimes dead patches in hot weather
diseases.untreated: Every handling spreads it along the row.

steps.title: Remove infected plants
steps.instruction: Pull out mottled plants, handling them last.

steps.title: Wash hands and tools
steps.instruction: Wash with soap and disinfect tools between plants.
steps.rationale: The virus spreads on hands and tools.

prevention.title: Wash hands, no tobacco products near plants
prevention.detail: Cured tobacco can carry the virus.

lifecycle: The virus survives in debris and cured leaf.
Hands and tools carry it to plants.
Handling spreads it along the row.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: tobacco mosaic virus
